title: Equal-spin pairing at finite Cooper-pair momentum in $p$-wave magnets
abstract: The realization of Fulde-Ferrell (FF) superconducting states has long been pursued but remains challenging because of the large Zeeman splitting required. Here, we demonstrate that $p$-wave magnets can host equal-spin finite-pair-momentum states with $p$-wave symmetry, termed FF states, at arbitrarily weak fields. Our Bogoliubov-de Gennes analysis shows that, owing to the displacement of the Fermi surface, two equal-spin electrons in the FF states pair at the same energy, just as in the opposite-spin zero-pair-momentum states of the same gap symmetry. At zero field, the FF states are therefore exactly degenerate with these zero-pair-momentum counterparts. An arbitrarily weak Zeeman field lifts this degeneracy and makes the FF states the superconducting ground state, since they remain stable owing to their equal-spin nature, whereas their counterparts are suppressed by the formation of Bogoliubov Fermi surfaces. These findings identify the fermiology of $p$-wave magnets as a promising route toward long-sought finite-momentum superconductivity.
summary: This work theoretically proves that $p$-wave magnets can host stable, finite-momentum superconducting states (FF states) even under weak magnetic fields. By using the Bogoliubov-de Gennes formalism, the authors show that these equal-spin FF states become the true superconducting ground state, providing a promising route to understanding unconventional superconductivity in magnetic materials.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of realizing superconducting states with finite Cooper-pair momentum (Fulde-Ferrell states) in $p$-wave magnets without requiring a large external Zeeman splitting.
main_result: The authors demonstrate that equal-spin, odd-parity, finite-momentum pairing states (FF states) are intrinsically stable in $p$-wave magnets and become the superconducting ground state upon application of an arbitrarily weak Zeeman field.
method: The analysis relies on Bogoliubov-de Gennes (BdG) theory, performing self-consistent gap calculations and comparing the ground state energy of zero-momentum versus finite-momentum pairing channels.
model_or_system: The system is modeled as $p$-wave magnets on a square lattice, described by an effective two-band Hamiltonian incorporating hopping, chemical potential, Zeeman field, and $p$-wave exchange coupling. The pairing is analyzed using the BdG formalism.
key_observables: Superconducting gap functions ($\Delta$), quasiparticle energy dispersions, and the calculated ground-state energy ($F_{A1}, F_{B2}, F_{FF}$).
important_parameters: Zeeman field strength ($h$), $p$-wave exchange field strength ($J$), chemical potential ($\mu$), and interaction strengths ($U, V$).
main_assumptions: The FF states are assumed to be equal-spin, and the analysis is performed in the weak-coupling limit.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically shows the pairing channels, contrasting equal-spin finite-momentum pairing (FF states) with inter-spin zero-momentum pairing. Phase diagrams (Fig. 2) are used to map the energetically favored superconducting state.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the pairing instability by deriving and solving gap equations for various symmetry channels (A1, B2, FF). It establishes the energy degeneracy at zero field and uses the weak Zeeman field to select the stable FF state.
why_interesting: The theoretical framework for stabilizing unconventional superconductivity via magnetic order is highly relevant to understanding exotic pairing mechanisms in strongly correlated materials, which often share theoretical underpinnings with AMO systems exhibiting strong interactions.
